title: Interfaces and Composition
summary: Classes that implement interfaces, and building behaviour from parts instead of hierarchies.

steps.title: implements
body: A class can promise to satisfy an interface with `implements`, as in C#:
async send(to: string, message: string) { this.sent.push(`${to}: ${message}`); }

`implements` is only a compile-time check (it is erased). Because typing is **structural**, any object with a matching `send` works where a `Notifier` is expected, even a plain object literal. That makes test doubles trivial: no mocking library needed.

code: interface Notifier { send(to: string, message: string): Promise<void> }
options: Yes: the object literal has the shape `Notifier` requires
No: it is not a class
No: it does not say `implements Notifier`
steps.explain: Structural typing: a function with fewer parameters is also fine, since extra arguments are ignored.

steps.title: Composition over inheritance
body: Instead of `class AdminUserWithLogging extends LoggingUser extends User`, **compose**: give an object the collaborators it needs and delegate to them.
interface Store { save(key: string, value: string): void }
constructor(clock: Clock, store: Store) {   // dependency injection, by hand
const fixedClock: Clock = { now: () => 1000 };       // a test double in one line
Each part is small, swappable and testable. This is the same idea as constructor injection in ASP.NET Core, minus the container.

steps.title: Implement an interface
prompt: Write `class MemoryRepository<T extends { id: number }> implements Repository<T>` storing items in a private `Map`. `add` replaces an item with the same id. `all()` returns items sorted by id. `remove` returns whether something was removed.
starter: class MemoryRepository<T extends { id: number }> implements Repository<T> {
solution: class MemoryRepository<T extends { id: number }> implements Repository<T> {
template: const dojoR: Repository<{ id: number; name: string }> = new MemoryRepository();
dojoR.add({ id: 3, name: "c" }); dojoR.add({ id: 1, name: "a" }); dojoR.add({ id: 3, name: "C" });
Dojo.eq("all() sorted, duplicates replaced", [{ id: 1, name: "a" }, { id: 3, name: "C" }], dojoR.all());
Dojo.eq("get(1) after remove", true, dojoR.get(1) === undefined);

steps.title: Compose a checkout
prompt: Write `class Checkout` whose constructor takes a `PriceList` and a `Discount` (interfaces below) and has `total(skus: string[]): number`: the sum of prices, minus whatever the discount returns for that subtotal, never below 0.
Also write two discounts as plain objects: `noDiscount` (always 0) and `tenOverHundred` (10 off when the subtotal is at least 100).
solution: const subtotal = skus.reduce((sum, s) => sum + this.#prices.priceOf(s), 0);
template: const dojoP: PriceList = { priceOf: s => ({ tea: 30, cake: 80 } as Record<string, number>)[s] ?? 0 };
Dojo.eq("ten over hundred applies", 130, new Checkout(dojoP, tenOverHundred).total(["tea", "tea", "cake"]));
Dojo.eq("ten over hundred does not apply", 60, new Checkout(dojoP, tenOverHundred).total(["tea", "tea"]));
hints: Store both collaborators in private fields.
